subject: Close timeline fragility: heatmap + senior escalation request
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@meditech.com>, Meditech Procurement <procurement@meditech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Close timeline fragility: heatmap + senior escalation request

Rajiv / Meditech team,

Quick note after the sync this morning — the latest signal from procurement and security shows two blockers that meaningfully move our close risk from "medium" to "high" unless we take a short set of mitigations. I attached an updated MAP (MAP_v2_Meditech.xlsx) and a one-page risk heatmap (close_risk_heatmap.png) for context.

Top-line:
- SOC evidence ingestion is delayed by ~48 hours (vendor HR scheduling).
- Procurement redlines remain outstanding for 3 of 7 contractual clauses (pricing/term granularity).
- These two items together increase acceptance uncertainty for the planned Aug 31 close.

Asks (decision requested by EOD 8/22):
1) Do we accept a short close-window bump to Sep 10 to allow procurement + SOC to clear, or do you want Redwood to pursue an interim acceptance plan?
2) If bump accepted, can Meditech sign the attached MAP v2 which preserves the Canaries milestone (pre-prod run) on Sep 2 and shifts final acceptance to Sep 10?
3) If you prefer interim acceptance, will you accept a 3-day smoke test + conditional go-live with acceptance holdbacks?

Internal note to Marissa / Ben — I recommend escalating to senior leadership for credit/term approval if Meditech requests an extension. I do not want us to lose momentum; propose we hold a 30-min exec cadence tomorrow to finalize tradeoffs.

Attachments: MAP_v2_Meditech.xlsx (MAP with adjusted milestones), close_risk_heatmap.png (one-page heatmap).

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@meditech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Meditech Procurement <procurement@meditech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close timeline fragility: heatmap + senior escalation request

Thanks for the clear summary, Karthik. We appreciate the heatmap — helpful framing. Two quick points from our side:

- SOC scheduling is stuck because our external auditor changed availability; earliest window they proposed is Sep 1. That creates a hard dependency for formal SOC receipt.
- Procurement needs explicit language on acceptance criteria (what constitutes pass for the smoke test) and liability holdbacks if we do conditional acceptance.

We are OK with a short bump to Sep 10 if Redwood can commit to:
- A concrete acceptance checklist for the smoke test (no more than 5 items), and
- A documented rollback plan in case production behavior deviates during the conditional window.

Please have your team send the checklist + rollback plan by EOD 8/22 and we will review internally.

– Rajiv
VP, Digital Transformation
Meditech

Karthik — good capture.

I agree we should escalate. My recommendation to Sales Leadership: offer Meditech a 30-day credit (applied only if final acceptance slips past Sep 10) and hold the current list price. That gives procurement something tangible while preserving negotiation leverage.

If leadership approves, I'll draft the short amendment and route for quick signature. Also: we should lock the 5-item smoke-test checklist (Ben can own) and include explicit rollback steps.

Marissa

Date: 2026-08-23T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close timeline fragility: heatmap + senior escalation request

Looping in a brief tech mitigation plan. If we agree to a conditional go-live / smoke test, Redwood can: 

- Provision a temporary Dedicated pool for Meditech Monday–Friday (1 week) to run the pre-prod smoke tests in a controlled environment.
- Deliver a 5-item checklist (I recommend: API lat p95 < 350ms, end-to-end pipeline success rate > 99.5%, sample generation correctness on 20 test prompts, KV-cache hit rate > 85%, no PII exposure in logs) by EOD 8/22.
- Provide a rollback playbook (rollback to read-only mode + revert routing to staging cluster) and a 2-hour incident on-call window during the smoke test.

If Sales okays the 30-day credit approach Marissa suggested, Tech will prioritize the checklist and the temporary pool. I attached a short runbook excerpt to the MAP_v2_Meditech.xlsx workbook under the "SmokeTest" tab.

—Ben
Head of Platform Solutions
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-08-25T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Close timeline fragility: heatmap + senior escalation request — summary & exec ask

Lauren / Leadership,

Summarizing the thread and escalating for a quick decision: Meditech (deal D-74321) faces an external-auditor timing issue that pushes formal SOC receipt into early September. Procurement is asking for clear acceptance criteria before they will sign. We have proposed two parallel mitigations: a short bump to Sep 10 or conditional acceptance with a 5-item smoke test + rollback plan.

Recommended senior decision (please confirm by 10:30am PT 8/26):
- Approve the 30-day credit (applies only if acceptance completes after Sep 10).
- Approve the conditional plan: Redwood provisions a one-week dedicated pool for pre-prod smoke tests and delivers the checklist + rollback playbook (Ben to deliver technical artifacts by EOD 8/22 — delivered).
- Allow Sales to sign the MAP_v2 amendment and route a short addendum to procurement; we will hold pricing.

If approved, I will:
- Send the MAP_v2_Meditech.xlsx with the executive-approved amendment to Rajiv and procurement (DocuSign link below),
- Schedule a 30-minute follow-up with Meditech on Aug 27 to confirm smoke-test timing,
- Publish a short risk-watch note to the close log with the heatmap snapshot.

DocuSign (provisional envelope): https://app.docusign.com/envelope/0a1b2c3d4e
HubSpot record: https://hubspot.redwood/deal/D-74321

Thanks — Karthik
Director, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference
